label: Late-episode GO, ramps with trial after rewarded S2 / S2-belief
explanation: Fires only at GO in the last ~12 trials of the episode (timing alone R^2 0.25). Beyond timing, its magnitude is set by an interaction of how late in the episode it is and the last outcome: it ramps roughly linearly with ep_trial (about +0.17-0.23 per trial from trial 88) when the previous trial reached S2 and was rewarded, and more broadly when the previous trial was rewarded and the ideal-observer belief favours S2 (1-belief, -belief_lo). After an unrewarded trial, or with S1 belief, it stays near zero or small (about 2 after an unrewarded trial inside an S2-reward streak, which it under-predicts). The trial before last adds almost nothing once belief is included. The profile additive ceiling (all = 0.05) misses this because it ignores the timing interaction; the multiplicative terms give dev 0.75 / test 0.68 R^2 beyond timing, using only observed quantities (no value/policy). Remaining errors: over-prediction after a2 S1 r and rare transitions, and under-prediction in long S2-reward streaks.

issues: Score reproduced: the claimed 5 terms give test R^2 beyond timing 0.6849 (0.75 on dev), well above the additive ceiling of 0.05. The drop from dev to test (about 0.07) is moderate, not alarming.

The slope claim misreads the weights. 0.173 and 0.242 are weights on two separate terms, and the plain ramp term has weight -0.080. So after a rewarded S2 trial with belief near S2, the net slope is about 0.173 + 0.242 - 0.080 = 0.33 per trial, not '+0.17 to +0.24'. The step term (-0.81) and the -belief_lo term add offsets on top.

The unrewarded-in-streak miss is real but small overall. misses shows windows where GO after a2 S2 u has actual activation of about 2.0 against a prediction of about 0 (e.g. t97 2.03 vs -0.02, t99 2.10 vs -0.18). But the mean residual for GO after a2 S2 u is only +0.012. Adding terms for the trial two back, or for prev_reward==0 x (1-belief), did not fix it (test 0.6847 to 0.6868). This looks like the gate carrying over its own past level, which these terms don't capture, rather than a missed observed cue.
The over-prediction after a2 S1 r (-0.044) remains. Adding a term for last_is('a2 S1 r') x ramp, plus two more terms, only moves test to 0.6859.
'The trial before last adds almost nothing' checks out: adding a ramp term for rewarded S2 two trials back gives test 0.6852.
How much the observed-only restriction costs, checked with a future term: adding the agent's upcoming choice (action==2) x ramp raises test only to 0.693. So belief is a good stand-in, as claimed.
Simpler subsets support the label: ramp x prev_reward x (1-belief) alone with the ramp gives test 0.628, and ramp x last rewarded S2 alone gives 0.529.
